packs.title: River, Gates and Open Space
packs.promise: Explore river landscapes, garden entrances and a modern station beyond Okazaki.

q.s: Collect three ways a grove repeats itself.
st: Use an open path view or JNTO’s grove photograph. Keep outside the bamboo and low protective fencing.
Find a vertical stem, a horizontal joint and a crossing branch or leaf edge. Describe the direction of each without touching anything.
Choose which repeat feels closest together in your view, then keep the three directions and your choice as a small visual collection.

q.s: Collect a support, a span and a patch of sky.
st: Stop out of passenger flows, entrances and tactile guidance lines, or use the station operator’s design-concept or Grand Staircase photograph.
Find a vertical support, a diagonal or long roof span and a pane that admits or reflects daylight. Describe how each helps divide the large space.
Select the part you would keep in a three-shape sketch of the station and save your set. Exact sunlight and an empty concourse are unnecessary.

q.s: Make a small visual game from a lawn-side view.
st: Choose a comfortable stopped place at the lawn edge or use the city’s labelled lawn photograph. Keep the path and other people’s activities clear.
Draw three simple shapes from the view—perhaps a tree outline, a building block and a stretch of lawn. Rearrange them into a tiny puzzle in your own note.
Invent one rule for someone to trace between the shapes without lifting a pen, then try it yourself. Save your original puzzle and rule. No public performance or physical course is needed.

packs.title: Water, Shade and Small Discoveries
packs.promise: Make a quieter Kyoto memory from canal textures, curved façades and a few words under the trees.

q.s: Collect a ripple, a rough edge and something growing.
st: Choose a roomy stopping place on the public pavement, behind the protective boundary and clear of people crossing the bridge.
Find three different textures: water, stonework and a leaf or branch. Notice each with your eyes; nothing needs to be touched.
Give each texture one descriptive word, then choose the strongest contrast between two of them.
Save your three words and the pair that made you look again.

q.s: Collect three rounded details from a preserved façade.
st: Find a comfortable public pavement view of the library’s older front, keeping its entrance and ramp clear.
Collect three curved details: an arch over a window, a sweep of decorative trim and a round ornament near the roofline.
Choose the gentlest curve and the boldest curve. Explain the difference using their size or shape.
Save the three details and your comparison. Reading the building’s lettering is optional.

q.s: Draw a little map of what caught your attention.
st: Find a comfortable public seat or standing place, away from a narrow path or event queue.
Choose three ingredients in the view: a path edge, a tree shape and a patch of colour or light.
Give each ingredient a simple symbol, then arrange the three symbols into a small map of your attention. If drawing is not comfortable, write three short descriptions instead.
Save the map or descriptions and name the detail you would return to first.
